note: Inspector's own always-true list: the promises this project makes, whichever task is in flight. Seeded by inference from the project's own tests (issue #24) and NOT yet confirmed by a person - every line is confirmed:false until the owner accepts it. No line carries a falsifier yet, so `inspector always` reports every one of them as not-runnable and posts error rather than success: check 3 brings up an HTTP app and mounts no repository, and Inspector is a command-line tool with no app to bring up. A line becomes runnable when it can be falsified from inside that boundary.

promises.promise: A project's check command never runs on the machine that invoked inspector. With no usable Docker, inspector refuses loudly instead of falling back to running it directly.

A check command cannot modify tracked source: every tracked top-level entry of the commit under check is mounted read-only, so a check that edits the code it is being judged on fails rather than manufacturing a pass.

A check command cannot read the host's git configuration. Only an allowlisted [core] and [extensions] copy reaches the container, so nothing in a git directory that could carry a credential is readable from inside it.
A check command cannot write to the repository's history: git is reachable for reading inside the container and a commit from there fails.
A check command that outlives its timeout is killed along with every process it forked, and whether that kill actually worked is read back from Docker rather than assumed.
A red result publishes nothing: no staging push, no commit status, no branch update. The local report is the whole record.
A green result is staged and stamped before the pull request branch moves, so the gate's first look at that branch already finds the status on its exact head commit.
The branch inspector may move is always named explicitly by the caller, is never read from checkout or tracking state, and may never be the remote default branch.
A branch whose history was rewritten locally is only published when the caller names the exact remote commit being replaced, and a remote sitting anywhere else is refused with nothing pushed.

Only GitHub's documented 201 Created counts as a recorded status. A redirect, any other 2xx, or a server failure after the request was written is never reported as success, and an ambiguous one is reported as stamp sent, outcome unconfirmed.
Anything that is not a verdict attempt at all - help, an unrecognized flag, bad usage - exits 64, so no caller can mistake it for green, red, or a refusal.

The examiner container receives only the permitted inputs - request text, feature map, always-true list, changed file names, pre-task test versions - and never the repository, an implementation diff, or any worker-written file content.
No capability is marked confirmed without a successfully delivered, recorded observation, and an untested capability never hides a found bug.
A reviewer finding names a file and a new-file line number from the supplied diff; a finding naming a file outside that diff is rejected rather than recorded.

promises.promise: Whichever model vendor was asked - including the unflagged default - is recorded explicitly in the report and in the posted status, so the choice can never be read off as nothing.
No file under the sealed agent's source tree carries binary content, so nothing that runs inside that container is unreviewable by construction.
